# Option-row taxonomy -- 008 Setup phase re-measurement

- Generated: `2026-08-15T00:00:00Z`
- Retires risk **R-C** (partially -- see Methodology), sizes Open Decisions **O1** (with
  `reports/equipment-taxonomy/2026-08-15.md`) and **O2**

**Non-destructive, and text-free.** Nothing under `data/`, `curation/`, or `state/` was written by
this report. No source sentence, fragment, or item name appears on this page. It carries counts,
class labels, and datasheet ids only.

## Methodology -- read this before the numbers below

This sandboxed implementation environment has GitHub access but **no route to wahapedia.ru**, and
is instructed never to fetch it ad hoc. `tools/option_taxonomy.py::measure()` (the live-acquisition
path) could therefore not be re-run here. Per this feature's own governing instructions, this
report instead uses the following **committed and published** evidence, all already governed by
the pipeline's own ordinary acquisition:

1. **`reports/footnote-restriction-taxonomy/2026-08-14.md`** -- the most recent **live** run of the
   options grammar's own diagnosis classes (`head_ok_no_verb`, `no_head_match`,
   `refused_conditional_or_equipment_qualified`), over the **current-size corpus** (2422 option
   rows). Restated in Section (a) below, **carried forward rather than re-measured**.
2. **`reports/option-taxonomy/2026-08-10.md`** -- the last live run of the finer 13-class
   `classify()` breakdown, over a **smaller, stale corpus** (1680 datasheets, 2452 rows -- this
   corpus has since grown by ~24%). Its classes 3/4/5/7/8/10/12 are restated in Section (a) as
   historical context for *which verb shapes* compose `head_ok_no_verb`, **not** as a current
   measurement.
3. **`data/wh40k-11e/`** and **`reports/wh40k-11e-2026-08-3/report.json`** -- this checkout's own
   committed curated tree and retained validation report for the published `wh40k-11e-2026-08-3`
   version (sha256 `3aa1043d580780db05696024b42dfcd8cc5e7daf621db991b04df27aec4adebf`, matches the
   GitHub Release asset exactly). Sections (b), (c), T003, and T004 below are **genuinely computed**
   from these by `tools/option_taxonomy.py`'s new functions -- real execution against this
   checkout, not a restatement.

**A same-day corpus drift is visible and reported rather than hidden.** The footnote table (1)
measured 206 unparsed rows at 15:11 on 2026-08-14; the candidate report (3), built ~6 hours later
the same day, carries 239 `OPT-UNPARSED` findings. This 33-row (16%) same-day movement is exactly
what risk **R-C** predicts -- the live corpus moves between runs -- and is why Section (a) below is
marked carried-forward rather than current, and why T003's census is stated as a bounded estimate
rather than an exact count.

**R-C is therefore partially, not fully, retired by this report.** The classes Phase 3/4 build
against (`head_ok_no_verb`'s six verb shapes) are confirmed present and dominant by two independent
live measurements four days apart, in consistent shares despite the corpus growing ~24% between
them. A fresh live diagnosis-class run, the moment
this environment (or CI) has a route to the corpus, is the concrete residual action this report
leaves for **T074**'s mid-campaign dry-run to close precisely -- T074 already re-measures the whole
census against the real corpus before a single override is authored, which is exactly the check
this report's own uncertainty calls for.

## Section (a): the disjoint class table, re-measured (carried forward -- see Methodology)

### Current corpus, diagnosis-class level (`reports/footnote-restriction-taxonomy/2026-08-14.md`, live, 2026-08-14T15:11Z)

| Class | Rows | Share of unparsed |
|---|---:|---:|
| `head_ok_no_verb` | 139 | 67.5% |
| `refused_conditional_or_equipment_qualified` | 50 | 24.3% |
| `no_head_match` | 17 | 8.3% |
| **Total unparsed** | **206** | 100% |

Corpus: 2422 option rows, 206 unparsed (8.5%).

### Historical context: which verb shapes compose `head_ok_no_verb` (`reports/option-taxonomy/2026-08-10.md`, live, stale/smaller corpus -- 1680 datasheets, 571 unparsed of 2452)

| Class | Shape | Rows (2026-08-10 corpus) | Phase this feature builds |
|---|---|---:|---|
| 3 | Distributive equip -- `can each be equipped with` | 34 | 3 |
| 4 | Active-voice replace, per-unit -- `can replace its/their ... with` | 31 | 3 |
| 5 | Non-distributive `can have ... replaced with` | 30 | 3 |
| 7 | Active-voice replace, distributive -- `can each replace ... with` | 18 | 4 |
| 8 | Item-subject passive -- `... can each be replaced with` | 13 | 4 |
| 10 | Pure grant, no replacement -- `... can have INT [ITEM]` | 9 | 4 |
| 12 | Upstream typo | 3 | none (rule 5) |
| **Sum** | | **138** | |

**Confirms, does not correct, Phase 3/4's ordering.** 138 (stale corpus, 2026-08-10) against 139
`head_ok_no_verb` (current corpus, 2026-08-14) is a 1-row difference despite 24% corpus growth --
strong evidence the *share* this class occupies is stable even though the live count moves, which
is exactly what a production ranked by measured yield needs to be true. **This report does not
re-derive per-verb-class shares against the current corpus** (that would require a live
`classify()` run this environment cannot make); Phase 3/4 should treat the 2026-08-10 relative
ordering (3 > 4 > 5 > 7 > 8 > 10, 12 gets no production) as provisional, confirmed by T074's
mid-campaign dry-run before Phase 5/7 commit further work on its strength alone.

## Section (a2): class 11/13 restatement -- `no_head_match`'s composition

2026-08-10's classes 11 (`Footnote fragment extracted as its own row (extractor bug)`, 8 rows) and
13 (`Residual unclassified`, 8 rows) summed to 16 of that corpus's measured `no_head_match`-shaped
residual -- consistent with the current corpus's 17 `no_head_match` rows (footnote table). Carried
forward as the basis for T043's Phase 4 finding ("predominantly extractor artifacts, routes to
Phase 7 override authoring") -- not re-derived here for the same reason as Section (a).

**T043 execution note (2026-08-17, Phase 4/US2 session).** Per rule 5 (tasks.md: "one production
per measured shape, and none for a shape measured at zero"), `_COMPLETION_HEADS` in
`pipeline/parse/options_grammar.py` stays empty after Phase 4. Classes 11 and 13 are extractor bugs
and unclassified residual respectively, not grammar gaps -- there is no clause vocabulary to write
a production against, only a smaller number of rows for a human to read against the source card.
This residual (17 `no_head_match` rows, GF23's three synthetic carriers proving the decision holds
structurally in `tests/enrichment/test_options_grammar.py`) is confirmed, not merely carried
forward, to route to Phase 7's override-authoring worklist (T071/T072) rather than to a Phase 4
production. FR-005 is satisfied by this measurement, exactly as it names: "measuring, not shipping
a production per row."

| 239 | 147 | 92 |

| 3 | 24 |
| 4 | 2 |

**Estimate, not a measurement** (this report's methodology note explains why an exact per-row diagnosis is not available in this environment): of the 92 single-unparsed-row datasheets, between **22** and **50** are plausibly blocked *only* by a `refused_conditional_or_equipment_qualified` row that no production or override may legitimately close (FR-006, O2) — bounded by the measured 50 conditional rows of 206 total unparsed (the diagnosis-class run this figure is carried forward from; see methodology note) applied to the single-row population, and by simple concentration.

**Compared against SC-002's headroom of 21** (a gain of 126 datasheets is needed from a partial population of 162, of which 15 are excluded by the spec as the item-constraint vocabulary gap, leaving 147 addressable and only 126 of those needing to close): **even the low end of the estimate (22) exceeds the headroom (21)** — this report's own reading is that SC-002's 98% is not reachable as written without either the override path closing the gap (which O2 rules out for genuinely conditional rows) or a restated ceiling, which this report states as its own finding rather than rounding it away — see T014's decision package.
